title: Platform systems & services: dashboards, runbooks, retrospectives, and roadmap (Q1 2027)
author: Ava Chen
content:
Overview:
This document consolidates Platform team working knowledge for systems & services, dashboard and alert standards, runbooks for high-impact services, a short retrospective of major incidents in the past 6 months, and the roadmap for Q1 2027. Use this page as the canonical reference for on-call, service ownership, and platform roadmap priorities.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: reduce time-to-recovery (MTTR), improve observability hygiene, and align roadmap work with reliability goals.
- Scope: core platform services (routing/proxy, model-serving control plane, batch workers, metrics pipeline, alerting/notification), dashboards and alerting, runbooks for P0/P1s, and cross-team coordination.

1) Systems & services inventory (high level)
- service: platform-proxy
  - description: edge proxy for API routing, rate limiting, and auth enforcement
  - owners: eng-platform/team-frontend (primary), eng-sre (secondary)
  - critical SLOs: 99.95% availability per region, p99 latency < 150ms
- service: model-control-plane
  - description: orchestration for model rollout, version pinning, and routing policies
  - owners: eng-serving-runtime (primary), eng-platform (secondary)
  - critical SLOs: rollout success rate >= 99.9%, config propagation < 30s
- service: batch-ingest-workers
  - description: asynchronous job processing for offline workloads (embeddings, bulk evals)
  - owners: eng-platform/batch (primary)
  - critical SLOs: job completion SLA 99.5% within window
- service: metrics-pipeline (prometheus+tempo+kafka)
  - description: telemetry ingestion, long-term metrics, tracing and alert dispatching
  - owners: eng-platform/observability
  - critical SLOs: metrics freshness < 90s, trace retention search < 5s

2) Dashboards and alerting standards
Intro: Dashboards should be task-focused (on-call, capacity planning, product health) and follow templated panels for SLOs, error budgets, latency, capacity, and cost signals. Alerts must be actionable, routed to an on-call rotation, and include runbook links.

Dashboard naming conventions:
- format: "{team} / {service} / {purpose}" (e.g., "Platform / model-control-plane / Oncall")
- required panels for an on-call dashboard:
  1. SLO panel (current burn vs budget)
  2. Availability heatmap (per-region)
  3. Latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99)
  4. Error rate (4xx/5xx split)
  5. Queue depths and backlog
  6. Recent deploys and config changes

Alert taxonomy and examples:
- P0 (paging): customer-facing outage, clear SLA breach. PagerDuty: P0-prod escalation. Example alert: platform-proxy_availability_drop > 0.5% sustained for 3m.
- P1 (paging, lower urgency): Partial degradation with clear mitigation path. Example: model-control-plane_rollout_failures > 5% in 10m.
- P2 (email/signal): non-urgent operational issue requiring attention. Example: metrics-pipeline_lag > 5m.

Alert rule template (example Prometheus-style):
  # ALERT: platform_proxy_high_error_rate
  # IF: increase in 5xx rate to >1% sustained for 5m
  # LABELS: severity=\"P0\", team=\"eng-platform\", runbook=\"platform-proxy-runbook\"
  # ANNOTATIONS: summary, description, runbook_link

3) Runbooks (P0 and P1 playbooks)
General on-call expectations:
- Follow the runbook and include the first 15 minutes timeline in the incident ticket.
- If no owner responds within 5 minutes for a P0, escalate to the SRE lead.

Runbook: platform-proxy (P0)
1) Detect: confirm alerts in PagerDuty & check the Platform / platform-proxy / Oncall dashboard.
2) Mitigate (first 5-15m):
   - a) If circuit-breaker triggered: disable offending upstream using admin API:
     curl -X POST -H \"Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN\" https://admin.internal/v1/proxy/upstream/{id}/disable
   - b) If CPU/GPU node saturation: scale proxies via K8s HPA: kubectl -n platform scale deployment platform-proxy --replicas=5
3) Triage (15-60m):
   - a) Collect logs: rtail -s platform-proxy --since 1h > /tmp/proxy-logs.tgz
   - b) Check recent deploys: gcloud container images list-tags ... (or internal CI link)
4) Restore & verify:
   - a) Re-enable upstreams after validation.
   - b) Confirm SLO panels return to green for 30 minutes before closing incident.
5) Post-incident:
   - a) Open incident ticket, tag related repos, and add summary to postmortem board.

Runbook: model-control-plane (P1)
1) Detect: check rollout monitor and error budget burn.
2) Mitigate: pause rollout (UI or api), failover to previous model version, and notify product.
3) Triage: collect config diff: git --no-pager show origin/main:configs/model-routing.yaml | diff -u - configs/last-known-good.yaml
4) Restore: roll back via: internal-cli rollout rollback --service model-control-plane --to <version-id>

4) How-tos (short guides)
A) Create a new on-call dashboard (5 steps)
1. Go to Grafana > New > Dashboard.
2. Use template Panel: \"Platform SLO template\" and set data source to prometheus-main.
3. Add required panels (SLO, latency, errors, queue depth).
4. Save as \"Platform / {service} / Oncall\" and set permissions to eng-platform and eng-sre.
5. Add dashboard link to service's runbook page.

B) Add an alert with runbook link
1. In alerting UI, create new alert rule and use service label and severity tag.
2. Include annotation: runbook: https://confluence.internal/platform-runbooks/platform-proxy-runbook
3. Test: simulate alert using promtool or firing test event and verify PagerDuty triggers.

5) Retrospective (last 6 months summary)
- Incident A (Dec 2026): platform-proxy rate-limiting regression after recent deploy caused 45m outage for one region. Root cause: incorrect default rate-limit multiplier. Action items: improve canary promotion, add automated integration test for rate-limit config, and add circuit-breaker telemetry.
- Incident B (Jan 2027): metrics-pipeline Kafka retention misconfiguration causing alerting gap for 24h. Root cause: config drift during a manual operator change. Action items: enforce config as code for metrics pipeline, add detection alert for retention mismatch.
- Outcomes: MTTR median improved from 28m to 18m for P0s; adoption of deploy-canary checklist increased to 85%.

6) Roadmap (Q1 2027 priorities)
- Q1-2027 Objective A: SLO-first observability (owner: eng-platform/observability)
  - Deliverable: SLO dashboard templates, automated error-budget alerts, and SLO export to billing.
  - Timeline: Jan-Feb 2027.
- Q1-2027 Objective B: Runbook automation and standardization (owner: eng-platform/ops)
  - Deliverable: Runbook-as-code repo, automated verification tests, and a runbook linter.
  - Timeline: Feb-Mar 2027.
- Q1-2027 Objective C: Cross-region proxy resilience (owner: eng-platform/networking)
  - Deliverable: Regional failover playbooks, improved health-checks, and capacity headroom runbook.
  - Timeline: Mar 2027.

7) Ownership and SLAs
- On-call rotation: eng-platform on-call (Primary) \u2014 1-week rotation, weekend coverage included. Escalation: SRE lead -> Head of Platform.
- SLOs (summary): availability 99.95% for critical services; latency p99 targets documented per-service in service inventory.

8) Metrics & reporting cadence
- Weekly: reliability standup to review burn and outstanding action items.
- Monthly: reliability retrospective and incident rollups for execs.
- Quarterly: roadmap review and SLO rebalance session (coordinated with product).

9) Useful links and refs
- Runbook repo (templates): https://git.internal/redwood-platform/runbooks
- Dashboard templates: https://grafana.internal/dashboards/templates/platform-slo-template
- PagerDuty policy: https://confluence.internal/ops/pagerduty-policy
- Postmortem board: https://confluence.internal/eng-platform/postmortems

Appendix: Example alert annotation format (copyable)
- annotations:
    summary: \"{{ $labels.alertname }} triggered for {{ $labels.service }}\"
    description: \"{{ $annotations.description }}\n    Runbook: https://confluence.internal/platform-runbooks/{{ $labels.runbook }}\"

If you are updating this page: add a short change note at the top with your name and the date, bump reviewers if cross-team changes impact eng-sre or eng-serving-runtime.
